messages.author: ec1bc1bea8773650
messages.subject: Two scan qtl
parts:
Hello ,
I have a BC2F4 line and i want to perform a qtl analysis. First i did single qtl analysis with different method ( marker regression, standard interval mapping, haley_knott regression) i found same result  for the qtl position, qtl is on the same chromosome but now i did a two-scan analysis and I got this message.

mydata<- calc.genoprob(mydata, step=2.5, err=0.001)
out2 <- scantwo(mydata, verbose=T)
plot(out2, chr=c(1:7))
Avis: 56122 LOD scores NA, set to 0
Avis: 186 LOD score < 0, set to 0
Could you help me to understand why I have this message ? How can I have LOD score value equal to NA or inferior to 0? Could i trust the result?

Here it's seems that there isn't interaction between qtl on chromosom?

Cheers,
princia

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Two scan qtl
parts:
I think the NA and <0 values are likely for tightly linked pairs of positions, where fitting the two-locus model can be difficult.
How many individuals, and how many markers?

karl
